text:
sam: quick run of a new cloudburst-attn variant comparison across hw (A100/H100/L40S). seq sweep 8..2048, bsz 1/8/32, tested flash, paged-fused, and paged-only. noticed a throughput drop on H100 at seq=128 for fused-paged. pasting trimmed results and run notes.

sam: results (median latency ms per token) - trimmed table:
```
gpu,variant,bsz,seq,median_ms
A100,flash-vanilla,1,128,0.62
A100,paged-fused,1,128,0.59
H100,flash-vanilla,1,128,0.54
H100,paged-fused,1,128,0.92  # << big jump
L40S,paged-fused,1,128,0.87
H100,paged-only,1,128,0.56
H100,paged-fused,8,128,1.20
H100,paged-fused,32,128,1.45
```

sam: weird because the same fused-paged path on A100 is faster. suspect kernel fallback or memcpy path on H100.

mia: can you paste p50/p95/p99? p99 will show tail spikes.

sam: p50/p95/p99 (H100, paged-fused, bsz=1, seq=128): 0.92/1.40/3.8

aj: huge p99. sounds like occasional KV spill or evict thrash. was KV cache warm?

sam: warm run (10 iters to prime kv) vs cold: warm median 0.58, cold 0.92. so warm helps but still a step.

lee: did kernel selector log flip to a fallback kernel at seq=128? grep the runtime logs for selector events.

aj: try this grep to show kernel transitions:
```
grep -E "KernelSelector|fallback|memcpy_fallback|kv_spill" /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log | tail -n 50
```

sam: ran that, found entries: "KernelSelector: picked fused_paged_attn_v2 for seq<=120; fallback to fused_paged_memcpy on seq>120 due to tile_estimate>threshold"

sam: attaching the small trace snippet and flame output link (perf-bot uploaded).

perf-bot: upload: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/3412345678-cloudburst-h100-fused-spike (flamegraph + nvprof summary) :eyes:

lee: perf-bot flame shows heavy memcpy on the host-device path right after kernel launch when seq>=128. that implies kernel got compiled with an unlikely tiling strategy that forces extra device->host syncs.

am: (typo) aj: oh also check kernel binary size and registers for H100; register pressure could force spilling and cause higher latency.

mia: can we reproduce with just a microbench that toggles the tiling heuristic? i suggest running two microbench variants: one with selector forced to prefer small-tile and one to prefer large-tile. keep other params identical.

sam: scheduling rolling micro-runs now. command I'm running:
```
./tools/bench_attn --gpu h100 --variant paged-fused --bsz 1,8,32 --seq 8,16,32,64,96,120,128,160,256 --force-tiling small,large --iters 50 --kv-warm 10
```

aj: also log the kernel metadata: set env REDWOOD_RT_DEBUG=kernel:selector,kernel:meta and attach the kernel names.

sam: will do. quick note: we should add an automatic regression check in CI for median_latency delta > 20% vs baseline for seq in [96,160] on H100. this case would have triggered an alert.

lee: agree. plus add a check for p99 > 2x baseline. that's what bit us here.

perf-bot: baseline compare job queued: https://ci.redwood/job/attn-baseline-compare/3412345678 (will post result)

sam: ok i'll post the microbench logs when done. planning to run A100/H100/L40S parity and then file a kernel-selector change with reproducer. thanks for triage. :thumbsup:

mia: thanks — if you need infra, I can spin a dedicated H100 for a few hours.

sam: grabbing the dedicated node now. back in ~2h with artifacts.

lee: quick reminder: also check quantized kernel variants (int8 path) — sometimes selector mis-evaluates perf cost when quant thresholds are close.

sam: noted. will include quant variants in the batch.

aj: nice catch. once we have reproducer we can update the kernel tiling estimator and push a small canary.

sam: closing loop later with results.
